STEP 1 - Vessel type: flat square plate (white, rim band visible, flat centre, no inner wall).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type: square plates are typically 20-30 cm. This one looks medium, about 25 cm across.
b) Reference: the plate spans roughly 430 px across the image width, and the food mound is about 200 px wide. No fork or spoon is in frame, so I rely on the plate type estimate.
Final width: 25 cm (area about 625 cm²).

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Romaine/leafy greens (Caesar-style, dressed): footprint about 12% of the plate = 75 cm². Thickness: loose leaves, about 2 cm average. Volume = 150 ml. Dressed cooked-style density 0.6 g/ml gives about 90 g. Caesar leaves with dressing are denser than raw, so I use 0.6.
- Parmesan shavings/flakes: about 8% of plate = 50 cm², thickness about 0.4 cm (two or three flakes stacked). Volume = 20 ml x 1.0 = 20 g.
- Croutons: about 4 visible pieces, plus some hidden. Roughly 8 pieces at 4 g each (bread 0.3 g/ml, each piece about 1.5 cm³ scaled up) gives about 15 g.
- Dressing (Caesar, thin smear over the greens): about 8 ml x 1.0 = 8 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: the greens are the base layer and are already counted. No deeper pile is visible, so no extra items.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g:
- Dressed Caesar greens: about 110 kcal/100 g (leaves plus dressing)
- Parmesan: about 390 kcal/100 g
- Croutons: about 400 kcal/100 g
- Caesar dressing: about 450 kcal/100 g

Totals: about 141 g and roughly 1,000 kcal... recalculating per item:
- Greens 90 g x 1.1 = 99 kcal
- Parmesan 20 g x 3.9 = 78 kcal
- Croutons 15 g x 4.0 = 60 kcal
- Dressing 8 g x 4.5 = 36 kcal
Total: about 173 kcal, 133 g.
